Slots.rationale: PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:18: `Slots = [first, second, third, fourth]`. The sim's `PhantasmalGardenersEncounter` (phantasmal_gardener.py:90-102) passes no `slots=` to the base `Encounter` either (`encounter.slots` stays the empty default) -- same representational gap as living_fog's, but here it is provably inert for a stronger reason: the GAMEPLAY-relevant consumer of SlotName for this monster (PhantasmalGardener.cs:103-106's `INIT_MOVE` ConditionalBranchState, `base.Creature.SlotName == "first"`/`"second"`/`"third"`/`"fourth"`, which picks each gardener's starting point in the BITE->LASH->FLAIL->ENLARGE cycle) is reproduced by the sim's OWN `create_monsters` override passing the identical string directly as a constructor kwarg (`PhantasmalGardener(hooks, rng, slot=slot) for slot in ("first","second","third","fourth")`, phantasmal_gardener.py:96-97) into an `init.add_state(flail, lambda: self.slot == "first")`-style conditional (phantasmal_gardener.py:64-68) that reads the SAME four strings the C# does. `SlotName`'s only OTHER C# reader for this class (`SetupSkins`'s tall/short skin pick, PhantasmalGardener.cs:76-81) is cosmetic. No sorting consequence either: all 4 gardeners are constructed together as the initial roster with no later slot-triggered spawn into this encounter, so `sort_enemies_by_slot_name` never needs to run on either side for this unit. Verified, not merely read: `test_underdocks.py`'s PhantasmalGardener-cycle tests (`py -m pytest test/test_underdocks.py -k Phantasmal -q`, re-run this batch, passed) exercise all four starting positions.

RoomType.rationale: RoomType.Elite. The sim represents room-type membership by pool bucket rather than a per-encounter attribute: `sts2_rl/rooms.py`'s `_underdocks_rooms()` places `"phantasmal_gardeners"` in `elite_keys`, which `seam/rooms_and_map` (the picker) and `rewards.GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` (keyed by `RoomType.ELITE`, see the gold-ladder guard) both key off. EXECUTED: `grep -n '"phantasmal_gardeners"' sts2_rl/rooms.py` -- present exactly once, in `elite_keys`.

HasScene.rationale: PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:22: `HasScene => true`. Presentation surface; waived per the monster tier's established precedent.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: The sim has no `Encounter.all_possible_monsters` field; the purpose this member serves (every monster class the encounter can ever field, including summons, for the obs vocabulary / bestiary-style previews) is served by `sts2_rl/vocab.json`'s `monsters` list, which every monster class the roster registers is checked into regardless of whether it starts on the field. EXECUTED: `py -c "import json; m=json.load(open('sts2_rl/vocab.json'))['monsters']; print([c for c in ['PhantasmalGardener'] if c not in m])"` -> `[]` (all present).

GetCameraScaling.rationale: PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:26-29: returns 0.85f, a combat-camera zoom factor. Presentation surface; waived.

GetCameraOffset.rationale: PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:31-34: `Vector2.Down * 40f`, a combat-camera pixel offset. Presentation surface; waived.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: C# PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:36-45 returns a fixed 4-element array, `(PhantasmalGardener.ToMutable(), s)` for s in ["first","second","third","fourth"] IN THAT ORDER -- zero RNG draws. Sim `PhantasmalGardenersEncounter.create_monsters` returns `[PhantasmalGardener(hooks, rng, slot=slot) for slot in _SLOTS]` where `_SLOTS = ("first", "second", "third", "fourth")` (phantasmal_gardener.py:26,96-97) -- same 4 instances, same order, zero draws. Slot STRING is preserved as a constructor kwarg (see the Slots guard) rather than as `Creature.slot_name`, which is a representational difference, not a roster/order/count divergence.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: n/a -- Encounter has no hook-listener interface
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by this unit. The sim's `Encounter` (monsters/base.py) is a plain dataclass with no `on_*`/hook-listener interface at all -- it is never registered with `HookSystem` (grep `hooks.register` across sts2_rl/: only `Creature.__init__`/`Monster.__init__` call it) -- so it architecturally cannot receive a combat hook, matching the false default by construction rather than by an explicit flag. Faithful.

guards.what: Gold reward ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, inherited from EncounterModel -- not overridden by this unit)
guards.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:64-100: RoomType.Monster -> 10-20, Elite -> 35-45, Boss -> 100-100 (both bounds equal), times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under Poverty. sts2_rl/rewards.py:170-174's `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` pins the identical non-ascension triple `{MONSTER: (10, 20), ELITE: (35, 45), BOSS: (100, 100)}`; rewards.py's own module docstring (line 32) states ascension/Poverty scaling is out of scope, matching this audit's own scope line (`PROMPT.md` Scope section: 'Ascension values: out of scope'). This unit passes no `min_gold`/`max_gold` override to its sim `Encounter`, so `generate_combat_rewards` (rewards.py:885-887) falls through to the room-type default range -- matching the C#'s own inheritance of the base ladder.

guards.what: Per-encounter Rng independence (EncounterModel.cs:41-49's own doc comment: the encounter's Rng is independent of the run's centralized Rng, safe because its state need not survive past the encounter)
guards.rationale: Stream IDENTITY (which Rng object, how it is seeded) is `seam/rng_streams`'s mechanism, not this record's -- cited, not re-verdicted, per PROMPT.md rule 3 and this batch's brief. What IS this record's to check: does the sim's draw actually land on that independent per-encounter Rng rather than a shared/run-level one? `sts2_rl/run.py:1702-1706`'s `create_combat` builds `encounter_selection_rng` via `make_encounter_rng(seed, total_floor, encounter.entry)` (rng.py, verdicted faithful by seam/rng_streams step 21) UNCONDITIONALLY now, on every path: `rng_set.seed` when parity mode is active (string-seeded runs, the conformance/replay path), `self._legacy_encounter_seed` otherwise (run.py:1704-1705) -- threaded into `CombatState`/`Encounter.create_monsters` as `selection_rng` (combat.py:240-243). REVISED from the prior pass: this record used to note that legacy/RL-training runs (`rng_set is None`) fell back to the shared `random.Random`, breaking the game's independence guarantee in that mode. That is no longer true -- `run.py:1694-1701`'s own comment now frames the shared-stream fallback as the PRIOR behavior ('before that it took create_monsters' selection_rng=None arm ... which the game's own isolation guarantee forbids'), and `create_combat` computes an independent per-encounter Rng regardless of `rng_set`. `grep -n rng_set sts2_rl/run_env.py` still returns zero hits (RL training sets no `rng_set`), but it no longer matters: the encounter-selection stream is independent on both paths now. No live or dormant gap here; if anything the prior caveat is moot.
